description:
The open-source multi-agent terminal where Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Qwen work together as a team — without your source code leaving the machine.

Termpolis is a cross-platform desktop terminal manager (Windows, macOS, Linux) built on Electron + React + TypeScript with node-pty powering the underlying shells. It ships as a native app, code signed on Windows, notarized on macOS.
What makes it different:
- Secure AI-assisted development. Built-in AI Security Center auto-scans every AI prompt against 70+ secret patterns, enforces Gemini paid-tier mode, and keeps an auditable JSONL log of every AI-agent terminal launch — every check runs locally.
- Multi-agent swarm. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Qwen Code work together on a task. A dedicated Claude Code instance acts as the conductor.
- MCP server baked in. AI agents control Termpolis via Model Context Protocol, open terminals, run commands, send messages.
- Transparent routing. Every subtask shows which agent got it, why, and what it cost.
- Activity observability. Every token, every tool call, every message from every agent is visible in real time.
- Intervention controls. Pause, cancel, or steer any agent mid-task without leaving the feed.
- Shared memory. A RAG-backed memory store that any agent can read and write via MCP.
- MCP-native end to end. All four agents speak MCP — no terminal-output parsers, no glue scripts, no bridge code paths.
- Share-ready output. One shortcut from terminal to Slack, Teams, or a PR — see Copy for Slack / Teams / PRs.
Termpolis now asks first
Your agents' configs. Termpolis connects to Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI only with your consent.
- The first step of the first-run tour lists exactly what it writes, with a Connect agents toggle. Skip tour keeps what the step shows.
- Updating from an earlier version? A one-time dialog asks you. Your current setup keeps working until you answer.
- Settings ▸ Agent Integration has an on/off toggle and a Disconnect button that removes everything Termpolis wrote. Uninstalling on Windows does the same; on any platform, Termpolis --disconnect-agents does it from the command line.
- The mcp__termpolis__* wildcard permission is gone, from new and existing configs. An explicit list of read-only and memory tools replaces it; every other Termpolis tool asks first.
- Termpolis never trusts your home folder or a drive root on an agent's behalf, and leaves the Codex approval settings you chose alone.
- It no longer writes AGENTS.md into your repos, and the duplicate Claude Code plugin is removed.
- Folders an earlier version trusted stay trusted, because nothing recorded which ones Termpolis trusted. The exceptions are your home folder, the folders above it and drive roots: v1.49 withdraws trust from those.
Approval prompts are yours. Termpolis no longer answers permission prompts, MCP-server approvals, [Y/n] questions or numbered choices. It confirms an agent's folder-trust prompt only when your agents are connected and neither the folder nor its git root is your home folder or a drive root. On first-run screens it still presses Enter and takes the default: Claude Code's intro splash, its theme and login-method pickers, and Gemini CLI's terms and sign-in screens.
Telemetry is off unless you turn it on. Settings ▸ General ▸ Privacy has two separate switches: crash reports, and a daily anonymous ping that carries only the app version. Skipping the tour leaves both off. A yes given to an earlier version doesn't carry over: Termpolis sends nothing until you answer once more, and both switches start off. Crash minidumps are no longer uploaded.
The token-saving proxy has an off switch: Settings ▸ Token Savings ▸ Claude Code compression proxy. It stays on by default, steps aside by itself when you already route Anthropic traffic (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, an HTTP(S) proxy, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry), and no longer rewrites tool inputs.
Second Opinion is read-only. It no longer runs the reviewing agent with --dangerously-skip-permissions.
Full Changelog: https://github.com/codedev-david/termpolis/compare/v1.48.0...v1.49.0
